answer: Each identity registers one copper pipe run at a jetty berth on a shale bedding strip, and posts an 80-credit bond. An auditor pressure-tests it and recomputes its drop from a public table of diameter, length, and flow; a leak or out-of-tolerance drop burns the bond. Fees rise with queue: first 32, kth 32+5(k-1), 1000th 5027, so 1000 fakes pay 2,529,500 plus 80,000 locked bonds, while honest pays 32 once and recovers the bond on passing. A rented-pipe ring fails because the copper serial, shale bedding photo, and pressure signature bind one key, so one jetty pipe cannot serve two identities.
